description:
Compare how two to five companies, people or entities are spoken of on podcasts, side by side: "how is NVIDIA spoken of vs AMD vs Intel?" in one call. Each subject's mention lines over the same window (default the last 30 days, at most 365) are grouped by their label on one speaker statement characteristics axis — `by="sentiment"` (default), certainty, specificity or temporal_orientation — and each label's share is of that subject's scored mentions, the lines that carry labels. A subject with fewer than 20 is marked low sample: read its shares as examples. By default it counts guests' and panelists' lines; `speakers="all"` adds hosts.

Each subject is exactly what `particle_podcast_get_share_of_voice` returns for it with the same arguments and `by` set to the axis, so the numbers agree. `breakdown` splits each label group by a second axis (how sure each subject's predictions are is by="temporal_orientation", breakdown="certainty"); `speaker_statement_characteristics` counts only lines said a certain way; `podcast_slug` or `publisher_slug` narrows to one show or network.

Pass every subject in one list, in the order to show them: a subject that matches nothing, or has no knowledge-graph entity, is an error naming it, never a silent zero. Not for who says it by occupation (`particle_podcast_get_share_of_voice`, one subject at a time), for the lines themselves (`particle_podcast_find_mentions` with the same speaker_statement_characteristics), or for mention volume over time (`particle_podcast_get_mention_trends`).

breakdown.description: Also split each label group by a second axis: by='temporal_orientation' with breakdown='certainty' is how sure each subject's predictions are. Must differ from by.

by.description: The axis whose labels each subject's lines are grouped by: 'sentiment' (default; how negatively or positively each is spoken of), 'certainty', 'specificity' or 'temporal_orientation'.

company_slugs.description: Two to five company slugs or domains from particle_company_resolve, in the order to compare them (e.g. ["nvidia", "amd", "intel"]). One of company_slugs, person_slugs or entity_slugs is required.

entity_slugs.description: Two to five knowledge-graph entity slugs from particle_entity_resolve for anything that isn't a person or company (e.g. ["germany", "france"]).

include_ads.description: Count mentions inside ad reads too. Off by default: ad copy is not a speaker's voice.

output_format.description: Output serialization. 'markdown' (default) returns the LLM-facing rendering. 'json' returns the structured payload as JSON text — use only for programmatic chaining where exact field extraction matters; the JSON shape is larger and noisier for an LLM to read.

person_slugs.description: Two to five person slugs from particle_person_resolve, in the order to compare them (e.g. ["sam-altman", "dario-amodei"]).

podcast_slug.description: Only mentions inside this podcast (slug from particle_podcast_resolve).

published_after.description: Only episodes published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 30 days before published_before; the window may span at most 365 days.

published_before.description: Only episodes published on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to now.

publisher_slug.description: Only mentions on podcasts of this publisher (network), by slug.

speaker_statement_characteristics.description: Count only mentions said a certain way, for every subject: {"temporal_orientation": ["future"]} compares how each subject's predictions lean. Labels listed for one axis match any of them; axes combine with AND, so add only the axes the request names.

certainty.description: How sure the speaker sounds. 'confident' for flat assertions and high conviction; 'hedged' for maybe, I think, it could, and other hedging; 'neutral' for neither.

sentiment.description: The statement's tone. 'positive' for optimistic, bullish, approving or praising lines; 'negative' for skeptical, bearish, critical or worried ones; 'neutral' for lines that clearly lean neither way.

specificity.description: Whether the line commits to something concrete. 'specific' for names, numbers, dates and mechanisms (concrete claims); 'vague' for generalities; 'neutral' for neither.

temporal_orientation.description: Where the line points in time. 'future' for predictions, forecasts, plans and expectations; 'past' for looking back; 'present' for how things are now.

speakers.description: Whose lines count: 'guests' (default; guests and panelists) or 'all' (hosts included).

name: particle_podcast_compare_share_of_voice
title: Particle Podcast Compare Share Of Voice
